biological.citation: Auto-fatty acylation of transcription factor RFX3 regulates ciliogenesis. (PMID: 30127002)
biological.summary: RFX3 undergoes enzyme-independent auto-S-fatty acylation at a conserved cysteine in its dimerization domain, preferring 18-carbon stearic and oleic acids. A fatty acylation-deficient RFX3 mutant shows decreased homodimerization, fails to promote ciliary gene expression and ciliogenesis, and impairs Hedgehog signaling. This links fatty acid metabolism and protein lipidation to RFX3-mediated regulation of ciliogenesis.

biological.citation: Multi-omic analysis of the ciliogenic transcription factor RFX3 reveals a role in promoting activity-dependent responses via enhancing CREB binding in human neurons. (PMID: 40060598)
biological.summary: Using human iPSC-derived neurons and forebrain organoids, biallelic loss of RFX3 disrupted ciliary gene expression and delayed neuronal differentiation, while monoallelic loss disrupted synaptic target gene expression and diminished activity-dependent gene expression. RFX3 binding sites co-localized with CREB binding sites near activity-dependent genes, and RFX3 deficiency led to decreased CREB binding and impaired induction of CREB targets upon neuronal depolarization. This reveals a novel role for RFX3 in shaping neuronal synaptic development and plasticity relevant to ASD.

biological.citation: RFX3 is essential for the generation of functional human pancreatic islets from stem cells. (PMID: 40263183)
biological.summary: CRISPR/Cas9 knockout of RFX3 in human iPSCs differentiated into pancreatic islet organoids reduced hormone-secreting islet cells, impaired beta cell function and insulin secretion, increased apoptosis, and elevated enterochromaffin cell markers. RFX3 overexpression rescued dysregulated gene expression in RFX3 KO cells at pancreatic progenitor and endocrine progenitor stages. These findings establish RFX3 as essential for human islet cell differentiation and suppression of enterochromaffin cell specification.

biological.citation: The transcription factor Rfx3 regulates beta-cell differentiation, function, and glucokinase expression. (PMID: 20413507)
biological.summary: In Rfx3-deficient mice, reduced insulin-positive beta-cells resulted from accumulation of incompletely differentiated beta-cell precursors with reduced insulin, Glut-2, and glucokinase (Gck) expression, leading to glucose intolerance in adults. ChIP and bandshift experiments showed Rfx3 binds the Pal-1 and Pal-2 regulatory sequences in the neuroendocrine promoter of the glucokinase gene in Min6 cells and human islets. RNAi-mediated knockdown of Rfx3 in Min6 beta-cells also attenuated Glut-2 and glucokinase expression and impaired glucose-stimulated insulin secretion.

biological.citation: The transcription factor RFX3 directs nodal cilium development and left-right asymmetry specification. (PMID: 15121860)
biological.summary: Rfx3-knockout mice exhibit frequent left-right asymmetry defects, situs inversus, and high embryonic lethality due to stunted nodal monocilia. RFX3 is expressed in ciliated cells of the embryonic node and regulates expression of D2lic, the mouse orthologue of a C. elegans intraflagellar transport gene. This establishes RFX3 as essential for nodal monocilia differentiation and left-right body axis determination in mammals.

biological.citation: RFX3 governs growth and beating efficiency of motile cilia in mouse and controls the expression of genes involved in human ciliopathies. (PMID: 19671664)
biological.summary: Using primary multiciliated cells from mouse brain, Rfx3-deficient cells showed impaired growth and beating efficiency of motile cilia. RFX3 was required for optimal FOXJ1 expression and directly bound promoters of axonemal dynein genes involved in ciliary motility. This demonstrates RFX3 regulates both ciliary assembly and motility genes associated with primary ciliary dyskinesia in humans.

biological.citation: RFX3 modulation of FOXJ1 regulation of cilia genes in the human airway epithelium. (PMID: 23822649)
biological.summary: In primary human airway basal cells, transfection of RFX3 alone did not induce cilia-related gene expression, but the combination of FOXJ1 and RFX3 enhanced ciliated gene promoter activity and mRNA expression beyond FOXJ1 alone. Co-immunoprecipitation studies demonstrated a physical interaction between FOXJ1 and RFX3 proteins. RFX3 thus acts as a transcriptional co-activator to FOXJ1 during ciliated cell differentiation of airway basal/progenitor cells.

biological.citation: Disruption of RFX family transcription factors causes autism, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, intellectual disability, and dysregulated behavior. (PMID: 33658631)
biological.summary: RFX3 (along with RFX4 and RFX7) is strongly expressed in developing and adult human brain. X-box binding motifs and RFX ChIP-seq peaks are enriched in cis-regulatory regions of known ASD risk genes. A cohort of 38 individuals with de novo variants in RFX3, RFX4, and RFX7 share neurobehavioral features including ASD, intellectual disability, and/or ADHD, establishing RFX3 as a critical transcriptional regulator of neurobiological pathways associated with neurodevelopmental disease.

biological.citation: Histone H2B monoubiquitination regulates heart development via epigenetic control of cilia motility. (PMID: 31235600)
biological.summary: ChIP-seq of mouse ciliated and non-ciliated tissues showed tissue-specific H2B monoubiquitination (H2Bub1) marks significantly enriched at the Rfx3 locus. Rnf20 knockdown in Xenopus reduced rfx3 mRNA levels and caused abnormal heart looping and defective left-right asymmetry, which was rescued by exogenous rfx3. This places RFX3 downstream of the RNF20/H2Bub1 chromatin remodeling pathway as a key mediator of cilia-dependent cardiac situs determination.

biological.citation: Downregulation of microRNA-342-3p Eases Insulin Resistance and Liver Gluconeogenesis via Regulating Rfx3 in Gestational Diabetes Mellitus. (PMID: 35997120)
biological.summary: In a streptozocin-induced GDM mouse model, miR-342-3p was upregulated and Rfx3 was downregulated in placenta and pancreatic tissues; dual luciferase assays confirmed miR-342-3p directly targets the Rfx3 3'-UTR. Knockdown of miR-342-3p decreased blood glucose, reduced apoptosis, and alleviated insulin resistance and liver gluconeogenesis, effects that were reversed by Rfx3 silencing. This identifies a miR-342-3p/Rfx3 regulatory axis relevant to gestational diabetes pathophysiology.
